notes.text: Cold morning outdoors, then dark around 16:30 while you are on the Shibuya Sky roof. Layers and gloves; trees are bare, the city lights are the show.
Cash for the flea market, the lucky cats and Gyōza Rō (cash only). Passports on you all day: tax-free needs ¥5,000+ per shop per day, paperwork at Haneda on Dec 29.
Check before the day: Shibuya Sky sunset tickets (release mid-November, all 8 in one order), the Uoshin room for 8, and KICKS LAB's opening time.

stops.summary: Out the door at 07:20 with konbini coffee in hand; the cat temple beats the crowds.
stops.story: Yes, it is early after a ramen-at-midnight first night, and that is the point: the temple and the flea market are at their best before the day-trippers wake up. Grab onigiri and hot coffee from the konbini on the walk.
how: Walk to Ochiai-minami-nagasaki for the Toei Oedo line 07:45 → Higashi-Nakano.
JR Chuo-Sobu local 07:59 → Shinjuku, then Odakyu line 08:12 → Gōtokuji 08:30.
76 min door to door, ¥540 on Suica.
tips: Passports and cash in pockets before you lock the door: you will not be back until night.
Taxi fallback is 34 min if the morning falls apart.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: The birthplace of the lucky cat: a wall of white maneki-neko, and you each buy one for the trip.
stops.story: Gōtokuji is where the beckoning-cat legend started, and the proof is thousands of white cat figurines stacked beside the Shōfukuden hall, all waving the same paw. Look up at the three-storey pagoda: there are cats hidden in its carvings. Free, quiet on a cold weekday morning, and very funny in a group photo.
how: Walk from Gōtokuji station to the temple.
Go straight to the cat figurines beside the Shōfukuden hall.
Hunt the cats in the pagoda carvings.
Buy your own maneki-neko at the temple office, then walk 14 min to Boro-ichi.
tips: Figurines run ¥300–1,500; cash.
The office selling them opens at 8:00 and supplies can be limited, so buy now, not later.
wishes: Legendary, not generic: nothing only there because it is on page one of every Tokyo or Kyoto itinerary, and no sit-down sightseeing filler between the big moments

stops.summary: A 440-year-old flea market that only happens four days a year, and today is one of them.
stops.story: Setagaya Boro-ichi fills a whole street around the Daikan Yashiki with about 700 stalls of antiques, junk, old kimono and vintage clothes, and it only runs on 15–16 Dec and 15–16 Jan. It is pure local Tokyo: grandmas haggling over teacups next to racks of worn workwear. Queue for daikan-mochi, rice cakes pounded on the spot, as second breakfast.
how: Daikan-mochi first, before the line grows.
Split into pairs: the street is narrow and packed.
Meet at the Daikan Yashiki at 10:45.
Tokyu Setagaya line from Kamimachi 11:09, then Odakyu and Chiyoda lines to Meiji-jingumae: 48 min, ¥490.
tips: Cash only in practice; small notes and coins make haggling easier.
Best before the lunchtime crush, which is exactly when you are there.
Bad weather can cut hours or cancel it: check the Setagaya city site that morning.
wishes: Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote and tax-free hauls
Be bold: prefer one-of-a-kind, local-run, hard-to-book and group-scale things, and name a safe fallback beside every hard-to-book thing

stops.summary: Kick off the Harajuku crawl at the atmos flagship and ask for the Japan-only pairs.
stops.story: atmos is the Tokyo sneaker shop that does collabs you cannot buy at home. A quick stop, one question to staff, and you know if anything here is coming home with you.
how: Ask staff for Japan-exclusive pairs.
Check the atmos app raffles a week ahead for any drop.
Walk 5 min to HUMAN MADE.
tips: Passport ready if you cross ¥5,000 in one shop.
wishes: Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote and tax-free hauls

stops.summary: HUMAN MADE's first global flagship: three floors, and the Tokyo-only pieces vanish first.
stops.story: NIGO's brand finally built its biggest store, and it is three floors of hearts, ducks and heavyweight tees in Harajuku. The Tokyo-only stuff goes early, which is why you are here before lunch.
how: Go straight for the Tokyo-only pieces.
Pay together per person to clear ¥5,000 for tax-free.
Walk 4 min to Gyōza Rō.
tips: Weekday close is 19:00, earlier than the other shops: do not leave it for later.
wishes: Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote and tax-free hauls

stops.summary: Cheap, fast, legendary: plates of fried and boiled gyoza and a beer in the middle of the crawl.
stops.story: Harajuku Gyōza Rō has been feeding shoppers forever with basically one thing, done right: gyoza, fried or boiled, six to a plate. It is loud, quick and costs almost nothing, which leaves more yen for sneakers.
how: Queue; it moves fast.
Order both fried and boiled: ¥340 for a plate of 6.
Weekday lunch set B (gyoza, rice, bean sprouts, soup) is ¥990.
Beers, then walk 6 min to KICKS LAB.
tips: Cash only.
Our hours come from an older article, so check it is open on the day.

stops.summary: Rare and deadstock sneakers: the shop for pairs nobody back home has.
stops.story: KICKS LAB is a curated sneaker boutique heavy on rare and deadstock pairs. A quick hit to see what the Japanese collectors are hoarding.
how: Browse the rare and deadstock wall.
Walk 9 min to Cat Street.
tips: Sources disagree on the weekday opening time; check before you go, though by 13:35 it should be open.
wishes: Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote and tax-free hauls

stops.summary: Free roam down Cat Street and the Ura-Hara backstreets for vintage and indie labels.
stops.story: Ura-Harajuku is where the actual style lives: small vintage shops, indie labels and 2nd Street for resale finds, along a car-free lane toward Shibuya. Spread out, find something weird, show the group.
how: Split up along Cat Street and the side alleys.
Hit 2nd Street for resale bargains.
Meet at the Cat Street end at 14:45, then walk 6 min to BAPE.
tips: Keep receipts per shop for tax-free.
wishes: Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote and tax-free hauls

stops.summary: Last shop of the crawl: BAPE camo and the Harajuku-only tees.
stops.story: The BAPE store in Harajuku is the mothership for the camo you grew up seeing on everyone's older cousin. Grab the Harajuku-only tee as proof you were here.
how: Ask for the Japan-exclusive pieces.
Keep it to ¥5,000+ per person per shop for tax-free, passport in hand.
Walk to Omotesando for the Ginza line 15:28 → Shibuya 15:31, ¥180; 17 min door to door.
tips: Do not dawdle: the Shibuya Sky slot will not wait.
Taxi fallback is 8 min.
wishes: Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote and tax-free hauls

stops.summary: Open-air roof 229 m above the Scramble: Fuji in the last light, sunset, then Tokyo switches on.
stops.story: Shibuya Sky is the one paid deck worth it: you are outside on the roof, not behind glass. December air is the clearest of the year, so on a good day Mt Fuji sits on the horizon as the sun drops around 16:30, then the whole city lights up under your feet.
how: Enter at 15:40 with tickets bought for all 8 in one order.
Big bags into the 46F lockers; no food or drink on the roof.
Find the Fuji side for sunset, then stay for the lights.
Walk 10 min to PARCO via the Scramble Crossing.
tips: Check the official page in mid-November and buy the second sunset slots open: they go within minutes.
Online from 15:00 is ¥3,400 vs ¥3,700 at the counter, if any are left.
Rain or strong wind closes the roof; tickets refund only if you have not entered.
stops.booking: Check: not bought until release (official site or Klook), all 8 in one order
wishes: Be bold: prefer one-of-a-kind, local-run, hard-to-book and group-scale things, and name a safe fallback beside every hard-to-book thing

stops.summary: Nintendo TOKYO, Pokémon Center, Capcom and Jump Shop, all on one floor of PARCO.
stops.story: PARCO's sixth floor is a single corridor of childhood: Nintendo TOKYO, Pokémon Center Shibuya, the Capcom Store and Jump Shop, back to back. Time here disappears.
how: Straight up to 6F.
Nintendo TOKYO sometimes runs timed entry when busy; check at the door.
Walk 6 min to Uoshin.
tips: December is full price: PARCO's big sale starts in January, after you leave.
Merch tax-free still needs ¥5,000+ in one shop.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Fishmonger-run izakaya: sashimi spilling off the plate, crab, overflowing nokke-zushi, free-flow drinks.
stops.story: Uoshin is run by fishmongers and has been since 1983, so the seafood arrives in piles, not portions. The star is nokke-zushi, sushi buried under so much uni and crab it slides off the rice. The course is ten dishes with all-you-can-drink, in a semi-private room for the eight of you.
how: Arrive on time for 18:30.
¥6,800 course: ten dishes including crab and nokke-zushi, all-you-can-drink.
Film the nokke-zushi pour.
Walk 5 min to Manekineko.
tips: Same-day cancellations or a smaller group can mean a fee; changes by phone only.
Check the booking says 半個室 (semi-private room) for 8.
stops.booking: Check it is booked: phone 03-3464-3000, ¥6,800 course, 半個室 for 8
wishes: Everyone stays together; every booking is for 8 at the same table or private room (8名で、同じテーブル/個室)

stops.summary: One room, eight people, free-drink plan, the anthems, and a hard stop at 23:40 for the last train.
stops.story: Manekineko is Japan's karaoke chain built for exactly this: a room for the whole group, a phone to order drinks without stopping the song, and a free-drink plan to make the duets worse. Leave on time and you get home by train; miss it and it's two taxis.
how: Phone-book one room for 8 (3+ people can book), or book on the shop page.
Join at the desk (members only) and take the free-drink plan.
Leave at 23:40: JR Yamanote 23:59 → Ikebukuro 00:14, Seibu 00:23 → Higashi-Nagasaki 00:28, ¥380.
tips: Joining asks for photo ID: bring your passport and check it is accepted.
Billing starts at 1 hour, then 30-minute steps; one drink each (¥451 or more) on top.
Missed the train? Taxi is 21 min home.
stops.booking: Phone or 来店予約 on the shop page
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly
